key_insight: HawkesNest provides a controlled synthetic benchmark for spatiotemporal point process models by independently dialing four latent complexity axes while keeping global rate and simulation cost fixed.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers a diagnostic testbed to pinpoint whether a model fails due to space–time coupling, background heterogeneity, cross-type interactions, or topology rather than unknown quirks of real datasets.
method: Built on a multivariate Hawkes process backbone.
Defines four deterministic complexity indices: space–time entanglement, background heterogeneity, cross-type interaction, and domain topology.
Uses controlled sweeps to keep rate, stability, and simulation budget constant while varying one or more axes.
evidence_signal: The authors report that the indices are monotone and nearly orthogonal under controlled sweeps, and that Hawkes-family baselines and AutoSTPP degrade under specific complexity increases.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is synthetic and generator-aligned, model rankings may not fully transfer to messy real-world STPP data with unmodeled effects.
paper_title: HawkesNest: A Multi-Axis Synthetic Benchmark for Spatiotemporal Pattern Complexity
